claim.pdf_says: D.19.4   Methods  /  D.19.4.1   General — printed at the same typographic rank as D.19.1 General, D.19.2 Classes and D.19.3 Objects, i.e. as children of D.19 Object oriented concepts.
claim.markdown_says: ## D.19.4 Methods  (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:45795)  and  ### D.19.4.1 General  (:45798), while the sibling clauses read '### D.19.1 General' (:45612) and '### D.19.2 Classes' (:45623) under '## D.19 Object oriented concepts' (:45609).
claim.why_it_matters: D.19.4 is emitted at markdown level 2, the same level as its own parent D.19, so in the heading tree it stops being a child of D.19 and becomes its sibling; D.19.4.1 then lands at level 3 alongside D.19.1/D.19.2 rather than under D.19.4. Any tool or reader that navigates by heading depth (ToC, section extraction for spec citations) mis-nests the whole Methods subtree. Annex D elsewhere does track clause depth correctly (e.g. '## D.14' / '### D.14.1' / '#### D.14.2.1'), so this is a defect, not the file's convention.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on four independent grounds.

(1) Nothing is missing, so the kind 'missing-heading' is a misnomer. Both headings are present in the markdown, in the right place, with byte-correct text and byte-correct clause numbers: '## D.19.4 Methods' (:45795) and '### D.19.4.1 General' (:45798), each preceded by a correct anchor (<a id="section-d-19-4">, <a id="section-d-19-4-1">). The rendered page-1138 work unit (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1138/page-1138.md) matches the PDF body text word for word, including the surrounding factory-object EXAMPLE and the CLASS-ID CheckingAccount code block. Not one character of normative or explanatory content differs.

(2) The claim's premise about the PDF is vacuous. I extracted the span metadata for PDF page index 1137 (printed page 1108) with PyMuPDF: the page contains exactly ONE bold face at ONE size — Cambria,Bold 11.67pt, 57 chars total, which is precisely the running header plus 'D.19.4   Methods' plus 'D.19.4.1   General'. I confirmed the same on the neighbouring pages: D.19.3.2, D.19.3.3 (p1136-1137) and D.19.3.4/D.19.3.5 are all Cambria,Bold 11.67pt as well. The 300dpi crop of the two headings confirms it visually — identical weight, identical point size, identical left margin. So D.19.4 and D.19.4.1 — a clause and its OWN CHILD — are typographically indistinguishable in the printed page. ISO's Annex D uses a single flat heading style for every sub-clause level; the only depth carrier on the page is the dot-numbered string. The claim's observation that D.19.4 is 'printed at the same typographic rank as D.19.1/D.19.2/D.19.3, i.e. as children of D.19' is therefore evidence of nothing: it is equally true of D.19.4.1, which is not a child of D.19. The PDF asserts no heading rank for the markdown to contradict.

(3) The claim's load-bearing supporting assertion is empirically false. It states that 'Annex D elsewhere does track clause depth correctly ... so this is a defect, not the file's convention.' I measured it across the whole transcription: of 305 numbered Annex D headings, 243 (80%) have a markdown '#' depth that differs from their clause depth; file-wide the figure is 1675 of 2474 numbered headings (68%). Markdown heading depth simply is not a depth carrier in this file. The cherry-picked counterexample ('## D.14' / '### D.14.1' / '#### D.14.2.1') is contradicted inside its own subtree a few lines later: '## D.14.2.3' (:44744), '## D.14.3.2' (:44801), '## D.14.3.3' (:44898), '## D.14.4' (:45047).

(4) The local evidence is misrepresented. The claim names '### D.19.1' and '### D.19.2' as the siblings that prove D.19.4 anomalous, while omitting D.19.3 — the immediately preceding sibling, same rank, three pages earlier — which reads '## D.19.3 Objects' (:45637) with '### D.19.3.1 General' (:45640) beneath it. That is the exact shape the claim calls a defect. '## D.19.3.3' (:45695) is the same, as are D.19.5.2, D.19.5.3, D.19.5.4, D.19.6, D.19.7, D.19.8, D.19.9.3, D.19.10 and D.19.11. D.19.4 at level 2 is the local norm, not an outlier.

What the claim has actually noticed is a genuine but GLOBAL property of the transcription pipeline — markdown '#' depth is unreliable throughout ISO_COBOL.md. That is not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy on page 1138, and it is not repairable page by page. If heading depth is ever to be normalized it is a file-wide mechanical reformatting driven by the clause numbers (~1675 headings), tracked as a tooling task, not logged as a spec-reconciliation finding against this page. For spec citation purposes nothing is at risk here: the clause number and heading text — the only things a citation resolves on — are exact.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-1138 discrepancy. Both headings are present with exact text, exact clause numbers and correct anchors; no content is missing or altered. The PDF prints D.19.4 and D.19.4.1 in the identical face at the identical size (Cambria,Bold 11.67pt — verified via PyMuPDF span metadata and a 300dpi crop), as it does every Annex D sub-clause heading, so the printed page carries no typographic rank that a markdown '#' level could contradict. The underlying observation — that markdown heading depth does not track clause depth — is real but file-wide (243/305 Annex D numbered headings, 1675/2474 overall), and includes the immediately preceding sibling '## D.19.3 Objects' / '### D.19.3.1 General'. Track it, if at all, as a single global heading-depth normalization pass keyed off the clause numbers, not as a per-page reconciliation finding.
